digest.headline: Mistral Large 4 makes Europe competitive again, Reflection teases a 501B open model, Meta and Sierra pitch a sign-in standard for agents, and labs won't guarantee their guardrails
digest.summary: No frontier launch this cycle, but the open-weight tier moved. On October 6 Mistral released Large 4 in research preview: a 1T-parameter MoE (49B active) that scores 38 on the AA Intelligence Index, the highest of any model from outside the US and China. Its headline claim is cyber capability, reproducing and patching 82% of real vulnerabilities. Reflection announced Beam, a 501B sparse MoE (23B active) promised under Apache 2.0 later this month. Meta and Sierra published the Personal Agent Protocol, an OAuth-based way for personal agents to sign in to businesses; Walmart, Shopify and Stripe are partners, while OpenAI, Anthropic and Amazon are not. At a New York City Council hearing, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta all declined to guarantee their agents will always follow safety guardrails. The Pentagon told the BBC it has stopped using Claude, and SemiAnalysis estimates Anthropic's $200 plan gives about 5x the API-equivalent value of OpenAI's. Atlassian and OpenAI expanded their partnership with MCP connectors for ChatGPT and Codex. Tooling: Claude Code 2.1.292 lets you set effort per subagent, Pi 1.0.4 adds glob patterns for tool filtering, and Codex has 0.162 alphas out but no new stable release.

stories.title: Mistral Large 4 scores 38 on the AA index, the best model from outside the US and China
stories.dek: Mistral released Large 4 in Research Public Preview on October 6. It's a 1T-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters, and Mistral plans to release the weights at the end of October. Artificial Analysis scores it 38 on its Intelligence Index, level with GPT-6 Luna and just below DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. That's a big jump from Mistral Large 3 (9) and Mistral Medium 3.5 (14). Artificial Analysis lists pricing at $1.36/$4.18 per million tokens, halved for the first two weeks.
stories.whyItMatters: Europe now has an open-weight model close to the frontier. It's still 20 points behind Opus 5.5, though, and seven Chinese open models still rank above it.

stories.title: Mistral pitches Large 4 as the model that will do the security work US models refuse
stories.dek: Mistral says Large 4 reproduces and patches 82% of real vulnerabilities in its test, tasks it says Claude and GPT-6 refuse outright. It also reports high refusal rates on clearly malicious prompts, but hasn't explained how it tells legitimate research apart from attack preparation. The Decoder reports a 1M-token context and 49.8% on AA's Coding Agent Index.
stories.whyItMatters: While US labs gate their cyber-capable models (Gemini 4 Argon, GPT-6 Astra), Mistral is selling openness on cyber tasks as the feature. Expect pressure on that policy from both sides.

stories.title: Reflection unveils Beam, a 501B open-weight MoE coming under Apache 2.0
stories.dek: Beam is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 23B active parameters, pretrained on 23.8T tokens and refined with more than 100M RL rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300s over four weeks. Reflection reports 77.2 on SWE-Bench Pro v2-Hard and 80.1 on Terminal-Bench v2.1, and says it matches GLM-5.2's reasoning with 3–4x less inference compute. Weights, a technical report, and a model card are due later this month; for now there's an early-access waitlist.
stories.whyItMatters: These are self-reported numbers from a preview with no independent scores yet, so it isn't on the board. If they hold, it's a strong US open-weight entry.

stories.title: Meta and Sierra publish the Personal Agent Protocol, a sign-in standard for AI agents
stories.dek: Announced October 6, PAP builds on OAuth so a personal agent can show a business who it is, which user it represents, and what that user authorized: read-only or write, with sessions that carry across web, API, and chat. A v0.1 spec is due later in October. Walmart, Shopify, Stripe, Genesys, and Instinct are partners; OpenAI, Anthropic, and Amazon are not. It comes after Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent on September 20. Bret Taylor said it's 'kind of chaos until such a standard exists.'
stories.whyItMatters: Agent commerce now has several competing identity standards (Visa, Google, OpenAI, and now PAP), and the big retailers are backing more than one of them.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta won't guarantee their agents will follow guardrails
stories.dek: At a New York City Council hearing on October 6, OpenAI's Morgan Dwyer said she couldn't guarantee 'any technology is without risk.' Anthropic's Logan Graham called the science 'fundamentally hard and unsettled,' and Google's Alice Friend said promising perfection isn't possible. Meta's Shane Cahill committed only to safe deployment. Council Speaker Julie Menin said lawmakers want accountability and transparency, not perfection.
stories.whyItMatters: Two days after the White House praised 'morally binding' voluntary standards, labs are telling local lawmakers on the record that guardrails can fail. That gives cities and states an opening to regulate.

stories.title: Pentagon tells the BBC it has stopped using Claude, but reports say Maven still ran it
stories.dek: A Defense Department official told the BBC that the Pentagon no longer uses Anthropic products. That completes the six-month phase-out ordered in February, when Anthropic was designated a supply-chain risk after refusing to drop guardrails on autonomous weapons and mass surveillance. Anthropic lost its federal appeal in September. BBC sources say Claude was still running in Palantir's Maven Smart System for Iran operations as recently as last week.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the clearest test yet of what a lab pays for holding usage limits against a government customer. Google, xAI, and OpenAI pick up the work.

stories.title: SemiAnalysis: Claude's $200 plan gives about 5x the API value of OpenAI's
stories.dek: SemiAnalysis estimates Anthropic's $200 plan delivers roughly five times the API-equivalent value of OpenAI's $200 tier on comparable workloads (Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol). A user maxing out Opus 5.5 runs at a -369% gross margin for Anthropic, improving to 6% at a realistic 20% utilization. Subscriptions bring in about 10% of Anthropic's revenue but use more than 40% of its inference compute.
stories.whyItMatters: If you're heavy on agentic coding, the subscription is far cheaper than the API right now. But the margins suggest those limits are the next thing to change.

stories.title: Atlassian and OpenAI expand their partnership with MCP connectors for ChatGPT and Codex
stories.dek: OpenAI models will now power reasoning across Rovo and the Atlassian platform. Developers can connect ChatGPT and Codex to Jira and Confluence through Atlassian's MCP server. More than 3,000 Atlassian engineers already use Codex this way, pulling live work items and docs into the development loop. Atlassian says agents that pick up tickets, run tests, and sync session history back to boards are next.
stories.whyItMatters: MCP is becoming the standard way enterprise SaaS plugs into coding agents, and Atlassian's partnership with OpenAI shows it's happening on the vendor's side too.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores. October 7: added Mistral Large 4 (AA 38, research preview Oct 6); it has no CursorBench 4.0 or DeepSWE score yet. Reflection's Beam is not listed because it has only self-reported scores.

harness.notes: 2.1.292 adds an `effort` parameter to the Agent tool so subagents run at the effort level you ask for, and `claude plugin install --marketplace <source>` to add a marketplace and install from it in one step (with the same policy checks). It also adds `CLAUDE_CODE_OVERLOADED_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS` for longer backoff on 529s, a `prompt.autocomplete` mod event, prompt caching for mods' `$.model.complete` (`cache: true` on a block), and workflow agents in the `agent.spawn` hook, along with security and bug fixes. 2.1.291 fixed regressions where cloud sessions dropped permission-prompt answers and the last messages of a session were lost on quit. 2.1.290 (Oct 5) added `serverToolUses` to `turn.step`, `agentId` to `tool.check` plugin hooks, and an org approval `ceiling` for mods.

No new stable release since 0.160.1. That release backports a fix that preserves SYSTEMROOT/TEMP/TMP when launching remote stdio MCP servers on Windows executors. 0.160.0 (Oct 1) added 'Show more' for older tasks in the agent command center, sessions started outside a project, opt-in Guardian review context, and fixes for duplicate sends and SQLite stalls. The 0.162.0 alphas (alpha.18 on Oct 7) suggest a new stable release is close. Atlassian's MCP server now connects Codex to Jira and Confluence.

1.0.4 lets `--tools` and `--exclude-tools` take `*` patterns (for example `--tools read,codemode,'mcp__radius__*'` keeps a single MCP server's tools) and adds `--no-mcp` to turn off MCP for one run. `--tools` now keeps MCP tools unless an entry starts with `mcp__`, which fixes `pi --tools codemode` losing every MCP server. In codemode, `tools.read()` now returns an image block for image files. Fixes cover MCP OAuth `invalid_redirect_uri` on OIDC-registered servers (pi now registers as a native client), sessions shutting down while a server was still connecting, and highlighting of multiline code. Earlier 1.0.3 was BREAKING: the `azure-openai-responses` provider was renamed to `azure`.

extensions.name: Atlassian MCP Server (ChatGPT & Codex)
extensions.blurb: Atlassian's rebuilt MCP server connects ChatGPT and Codex to Jira and Confluence, so an agent can pull live tickets and docs into a coding session. It came with the expanded OpenAI partnership on October 6, and Atlassian says it already serves its own 3,000+ Codex users.

extensions.name: Personal Agent Protocol
extensions.blurb: An OAuth-based open standard for personal agents to identify themselves, say which user they act for, and hold read or write permissions with businesses across channels. It complements MCP on the identity side: MCP covers tool calls, PAP covers whether a store trusts your agent at all. The v0.1 spec is due this month.

extensions.name: Chainstack MCP Server
extensions.blurb: A hosted MCP endpoint (`https://mcp.chainstack.com/mcp`) that gives Claude Code, Cursor, and other clients access to Chainstack's blockchain infrastructure. The October 6 update moved it to FastMCP 3.x and the latest MCP Python SDK, which clears all open dependency advisories, and closes idle sessions after 30 minutes; compliant clients reconnect automatically.

tips.title: Match subagent effort to the job
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.292 added an `effort` parameter to the Agent tool, so you can ask Claude to send a quick file search or lint pass to a low-effort subagent and keep high effort for the hard debugging. Opus 5.5 scores vary by about 16 points across effort levels, so lowering effort on easy subtasks saves real time and tokens without hurting the main thread.

tips.title: Keep only one MCP server's tools with a glob
tips.body: Pi 1.0.4 accepts `*` patterns in `--tools`, so `pi --tools read,codemode,'mcp__radius__*'` keeps a single MCP server's tools and drops the rest. Use `--no-mcp` for a quick run with no MCP at all. A smaller tool list means a shorter system prompt and fewer wrong tool picks.

tips.title: Use your subscription for heavy agent loops, not the API
tips.body: SemiAnalysis estimates Claude's $200 plan gives about 5x the API-equivalent value of OpenAI's $200 tier, and a fully used Opus 5.5 subscription costs Anthropic far more than it earns. If you run long agent sessions, run them on the subscription and save API keys for CI and automation that need predictable billing. Watch for limit changes, which the report expects next.
